column1: # index build cost over the multi-GB scale corpus, measured with /usr/bin/time -l
# corpus: shallow clones of linux, llvm, go, rust under
#   one scratch corpus root  ·  352316 files on disk  ·  5.5 GiB incl. VCS metadata
# The three engines do NOT see identical bytes, and the fairness contract in
# gist/bench/dominance/races/field.sh says so: gist and csearch index a text corpus filtered by
# their own binary/ignore heuristics, while zoekt takes no file list and indexes the
# roots tree. `text_gib` is therefore reported per engine as each one measured it, and
# `index_pct_text` is normalized against that engine's own text volume.
# gist's peak RSS was the honest weak spot of this table (14.50 GiB, 5.1x csearch) and is
# still not normalized away — it is now 4.56 GiB after the block-fired trigram builder,
# which is the whole reason this row was re-measured rather than left to age.

# gist's wall is the median of 5 reps on a box ~10 coworker agents were also building on:
# user time held at 24.8-25.1 s across every rep while sys swung 19-41 s, so the spread is
# the machine, not the builder. csearch's and zoekt's rows are from a quieter session, so
# the ratio derived against them understates gist's build speed rather than flattering it.
# gist also writes an 18.4 MiB paths sidecar (the doc->path table), counted separately.
# zoekt's index_mib is the on-disk shard total (8.7 GiB) measured with du -sh; its
# text_gib is the whole roots tree because zoekt indexed it without a file list, so its
# index_pct_text is a ceiling rather than a like-for-like ratio.
